correctness.rationale: The two-layer prism map is conjugate over F2[z]/(z^n+1) to [[a,0],[1,a]], a equal to the cyclic-shift inverse multiplied by the cubic-factor polynomial. For even t, T^t-I is diagonal, giving twice the relevant polynomial gcd degree. For odd t, local Smith factors are (1,(a^t+1)²) at every root of a^t+1, giving the relevant squared-polynomial gcd degree. Möbius inversion counts least-period cycles. For n=v or 3v with v=2^k, the periodic factor is exactly (z+1)^v and a=1+s with valuation_((z+1))(s)=2, so the closed fixed-period population formulas; all remaining cycles are powers of two. Bounds rim lengths at least three and odd time the first odd update time considered. Exact bit-matrix checks for n=3..44,the first odd update time..34, exhaustive labelled trajectories n=3..8 (87360 states), and independent polynomial-family checks 135 parameters through v=256 pass from actual embedded scripts. Computations are finite checks only.

value.rationale: Full least-temporal-period cycle counts are a natural invariant of deterministic finite dynamics distinct from and not implied by prior nilpotent/transient statistics. The theorem solves this invariant on all sizes of a common cubic graph family and completely classifies two natural power-of-two rim families. Its exact equality of recurrent orbit profiles for rims v and 3v despite different graph sizes is structural, and its unbounded largest temporal periods v/2 contrast with prior nilpotent-depth information. Value is the resolved explicit cycle census, not mere finite enumeration, a renamed Jordan theorem, or a generic Mobius deduction.
